answer: Think of identities as trees in a grove: each new one must lock a stake that rises with the operator count, so the nectar of trust is never free. The first identity locks 10 units, the second 20, the third 30, and the delta between successive stakes keeps widening the bill, so N fakes lock 5N(N+1) units in total. Cost grows quadratically, while one honest identity pays only 10.
